instruction:
Hot-Swap MOSFET Safe-Operating-Area Enforcement

/home/user/Desktop/hotswap_spec.csv defines a hot-swap startup scenario (V_in = 12V, inrush = 3A, t_inrush = 60ms, C_load = 200uF, C_slew_existing = 10nF). /home/user/Desktop/mosfet_soa.csv gives the MOSFET's safe-operating-area polygon as a list of (Vds, Id) vertices (closed polygon, in order). /home/user/Desktop/hotswap.kicad_sch holds the slew-control capacitor C_SLEW.

Determine whether the worst-case (V_in, inrush) point is inside the MOSFET SOA using a point-in-polygon test. If it is OUTSIDE, choose a larger C_slew value such that the scaled inrush current (I_inrush_new = I_inrush_old * C_slew_existing / C_slew_new) lies below the SOA's upper boundary at Vds = V_in.

Requirements:
1. /home/user/Desktop/hotswap_report.csv has exactly one data row with these columns: scenario, Vds_worst, Id_worst, point_inside_SOA, margin_pct, suggested_C_slew_nF.
2. Vds_worst approx V_in (within 0.2V) and Id_worst approx inrush (within 0.2A).
3. point_inside_SOA is a boolean (True/False) that agrees with the actual polygon check.
4. If point_inside_SOA is False, suggested_C_slew_nF must be strictly greater than C_slew_existing and large enough that I_inrush_new falls below the SOA top boundary at Vds = V_in.
5. /home/user/Desktop/hotswap_updated.kicad_sch is the same schematic as the input but with the C_SLEW symbol's Value property set to the suggested capacitance in nF (e.g. '22nF').

Write /home/user/Desktop/hotswap_report.csv and /home/user/Desktop/hotswap_updated.kicad_sch.
